profile.summary: SpliceAI2 is a deep learning model from Illumina that predicts RNA splicing from genomic sequence. It reads about 200 kb of DNA around a gene and predicts how much each position is used as a splice donor or acceptor, how much each splice junction is used, and the most likely complete transcripts. Comparing predictions for reference and alternate alleles gives a score for how strongly a variant changes splicing.
profile.summary_source_locator: Manuscript: Main 'Hierarchical model of RNA splicing'; Methods 'Variant effect prediction'; README: introduction

summary_quotes.text: We introduce SpliceAI2, a deep learning model that processes approximately 200 kb of genomic sequence to predict position-wise splice site usage and pairwise splice junction usage, and integrates these predictions to infer complete transcripts and their usage
A variant is scored by comparing predictions for the genomic sequences with reference and alternate alleles.
a deep learning model that predicts variant effects on splicing through quantitative modeling of splice sites, splice junctions, and transcripts.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: The input is 196,608 bp of genomic sequence on the gene's sense strand, one-hot encoded, plus a one-hot code for the species (ten channels). A dense layer projects it to 256 channels, and 20 MetaFormer blocks follow, each with a depth-wise dilated convolution and a feed-forward network, at progressively coarser pooling. Each block's output feeds a splice site head over the central 65,536 positions. The 1,024 positions with the highest splice site usage are then paired by a query-key product to give a 1,024 by 1,024 matrix of splice junction usage. Sites and junctions form a splice graph, and Viterbi decoding finds the highest scoring paths, which are the predicted transcripts. The model was trained end-to-end on splice site, junction and transcript usage, with the three losses summed.
sections.source_locator: Manuscript: Methods 'SpliceAI2 model' (Inputs, Architecture, Outputs, Training); 'Transcript prediction'

quotes.text: The model takes as input a 196,608 bp genomic sequence on the sense strand of the gene, represented as a 14 × 196,608 matrix.
The first four channels one-hot encode the nucleotide at each position and the remaining ten channels one-hot encode the species.
This representation is passed sequentially through 20 MetaFormer blocks
The token mixer applies batch normalization followed by a depth-wise convolution of kernel size 5 and dilation rate that doubles every two blocks.
Each of the 20 block outputs is cropped to the central 65,536 positions and reduced to two channels by separate dense layers.
The 1,024 positions with the highest splice site usage, taken as the maximum of the splice donor and acceptor usage, are selected
Transcripts are predicted by finding the highest scoring paths through the splice graph constructed from the splice donor, acceptor, and junction outputs.
Viterbi decoding recovers the top scoring path exactly in quadratic time in the number of candidate splice sites.
The total loss is the sum of the splice site, splice junction, and transcript losses

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The code is package version 2.0 (this page read commit 1dcd2a18 on main). The released model is an ensemble of two checkpoints trained with identical settings, held on Hugging Face as spliceai2_multispecies_13M_01 and spliceai2_multispecies_13M_02, each with a model.ckpt; the README's commands pass both folders. Illumina also publishes precomputed scores for all possible single nucleotide variants and observed indels in protein-coding genes (GENCODE v48, GRCh38). The manuscript also describes a tissue-specific model conditioned on RBP expression; the files read do not show it as released. A result should name the package version, both checkpoint folders and the Hugging Face revision (55948bae read here).

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: A dense input projection to 256 channels, then 20 MetaFormer blocks (depth-wise dilated convolution token mixer, feed-forward channel mixer) with multi-scale pooling; per-block splice site heads; a query-key junction head with rotary position embeddings over the top 1,024 sites; Viterbi decoding of a splice graph for transcripts. PyTorch Lightning implementation.

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: Splice donor and acceptor usage over the central 65,536 positions, junction usage for pairs among 1,024 candidate sites, and top-k transcripts. The scoring tool writes a spliceai2_summary_score from 0 to 1 plus 260 detail columns; recommended thresholds are 0.1 (high recall), 0.25 (balance) and 0.5 (high precision).

facts.label: Parameters
facts.value: Approximately 13 million trainable parameters per model, as stated in the manuscript; the released ensemble has two such models. Each model.ckpt file is 117,134,011 bytes (folder _01).

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: Splice junctions from 314,745 bulk short-read RNA-seq samples (67,493,026 junctions) in ten mammalian species, from recount3 and the NCBI SRA, restricted to protein-coding genes; plus transcripts from 330 ENCODE long-read RNA-seq samples (189 human, 141 mouse). Genes on human chromosomes 21 and 22 were held out for validation.

quotes.text: We compiled bulk RNA-seq data for ten mammalian species from recount3
yielding 314,745 samples and 67,493,026 splice junctions
comprising 189 human (GRCh38) and 141 mouse (GRCm38) samples
Genes on human chromosomes 21 and 22 were held out for validation, and all remaining genes were used for training.

facts.label: Known versions
facts.value: SpliceAI2 2.0: an ensemble of two checkpoints, spliceai2_multispecies_13M_01 and spliceai2_multispecies_13M_02, on Hugging Face (read at revision 55948bae). Precomputed scores are also distributed. It is the successor of SpliceAI, and the README maps SpliceAI thresholds and output columns to SpliceAI2 ones.

run_guide.summary: Install SpliceAI2 from the repository and score a TSV of variants with the two released checkpoints and a reference genome.
prerequisites: Python 3.10 or later (setup.py) with a CUDA-capable GPU, which the README says is required.
The two checkpoint folders from https://huggingface.co/illumina-ai/SpliceAI2, which is gated: accept the SpliceAI2 Model Terms of Use and give academic details. The sources give no download command.
A reference genome FASTA and a TSV of variants with columns chrom, pos, ref, alt and strand.
Licence: non-commercial organisations only, research use only, not for diagnostic procedures.

steps.title: Get the code and install it
steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/Illumina/SpliceAI2.git
cd SpliceAI2
git checkout --detach 1dcd2a1882a8223095e7529982ae70bcb658340a
pip install -e .
steps.explanation: The README's source install. The checkout line is added to pin the commit this page was written from. The README also offers pip install spliceai2 from PyPI instead.

steps.title: Score variants
steps.explanation: Replace the placeholder paths with the two downloaded checkpoint folders (spliceai2_multispecies_13M_01 and _02 on Hugging Face), the variant TSV and the reference FASTA. The README suggests adding --no_compile when scoring only a few variants or if torch.compile fails.

notes: The record already holds the README and LICENSE at the same commit 1dcd2a18 as existing sources; they were fetched again here so they could be quoted. The manuscript was read from the Illumina-hosted PDF linked in the README, not from the bioRxiv PDF in the record, and its text was extracted with pdftotext. The repository files are under Illumina's terms, which bar redistribution, so store_bytes is false for them and for the manuscript. The manuscript source sha256 is of the pdftotext output (artifacts/manuscript.txt), not of the PDF at artifact_url, so a re-fetch of the PDF will not match it; artifacts/manuscript.pdf is kept alongside but not listed as a source.
